finding: tests/test_signal_search.py:735 The derived-containment tests do not exercise the pre-pin directory-creation race.
rationale: The failure is unreachable because every artifact write in build_projection is descriptor-relative behind _pin_search_root (_signal_projection.py:129-130,136-167), whose immediate per-component O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY dir-fd walk of .anomaly/search (lines 658-667) fails with ELOOP on any .anomaly symlink swapped during the pre-pin window, aborting before any byte leaves the case root, while _directory_still_pinned (lines 155,665,675-682) rejects path/descriptor divergence by dev/ino; the residual effect of winning the race is only mkdir(exist_ok=True) creating empty directories at the attacker-authored symlink target with zero projection bytes and canonical inputs untouched (no-follow input reads guarded by the line-700 test), so a symlink-following mutant passes the existing swap/static tests because it is observably safe — the pin layer enforcing that safety is itself exercised by test 735's post-swap scenario — making the missing microsecond-window test defense-in-depth polish rather than a blocking defect.
